title: READ-002: Extract magic strings to constants
description: Token keys 'arcvault_jwt', 'arcvault_token', 'arcvault_user', and 'arcvault_remember_me' are repeated 8+ times throughout api.ts. Extracting these to a STORAGE_KEYS constant improves maintainability and prevents typos.

context.current_pattern: String literals like 'arcvault_jwt' and 'arcvault_token' repeated throughout code
context.goal: Extract to STORAGE_KEYS constant for single source of truth

acceptance_criteria: STORAGE_KEYS constant defined at top of api.ts with TOKEN, USER, REMEMBER_ME keys
All localStorage.getItem/setItem/removeItem calls use STORAGE_KEYS instead of string literals
No string literals remain in code (all replaced with STORAGE_KEYS references)
No typos introduced; all replaced strings match exactly

implementation_notes.optional_useAuth_js: useAuth.js can import STORAGE_KEYS from api.ts if needed, or define its own copy
implementation_notes.no_breaking_changes: This is purely internal refactoring; localStorage keys themselves don't change

code_review: Verify all localStorage calls use STORAGE_KEYS constant
Check no string literals remain (grep for 'arcvault_')
regression_test: Token persistence across page reloads works

rollback_plan: git revert <commit-hash> — isolated refactoring, safe to revert
notes: This refactoring enables IMPL-006 (JSDoc) and IMPL-013 (variable naming) to build on cleaner code. No functional changes; pure code organization improvement.
